🔐 Encryption at Rest

AES-256-GCM authenticated encryption for every page written to disk — transparent to your application code.

Overview

BLite 5.0.0 adds first-class encryption at rest via the CryptoOptions API. Every database page is encrypted individually using AES-256-GCM before being written to disk and decrypted transparently on read. The nonce (IV) is derived per-page so each write is unique.

When encryption is enabled the database file is opaque — even with direct filesystem access, data cannot be read without the key.

Quick Start

using BLite.Core;
using BLite.Core.Crypto;

var key = CryptoOptions.DeriveKey("my-passphrase", salt: myStoredSalt);

var options = new BLiteEngineOptions
{
    DatabasePath = "secure.blite",
    Crypto = new CryptoOptions
    {
        Key = key   // 32-byte AES-256 key
    }
};

await using var engine = new BLiteEngine(options);
var col = engine.GetOrCreateCollection("users");

Key Derivation

Use the built-in CryptoOptions.DeriveKey helper to derive a 32-byte key from a passphrase using PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256:

// Generate a salt once and persist it alongside the database
var salt = CryptoOptions.GenerateSalt();   // returns byte[32]
File.WriteAllBytes("secure.salt", salt);

// Each subsequent open: read the salt + derive the key
var salt = File.ReadAllBytes("secure.salt");
var key  = CryptoOptions.DeriveKey("my-passphrase", salt);
Never store the passphrase. Store only the salt. If the passphrase is lost, the database cannot be recovered.

Providing a Custom Crypto Provider

For HSM or KMS integration, implement IBLiteCryptoProvider:

public class AzureKvsCryptoProvider : IBLiteCryptoProvider
{
    public Memory<byte> Encrypt(ReadOnlySpan<byte> plaintext, long pageIndex) { /* ... */ }
    public Memory<byte> Decrypt(ReadOnlySpan<byte> ciphertext, long pageIndex) { /* ... */ }
}

var options = new BLiteEngineOptions
{
    DatabasePath = "secure.blite",
    Crypto = new CryptoOptions { Provider = new AzureKvsCryptoProvider() }
};

NullCryptoProvider (testing)

For unit tests or environments where encryption is optional, use NullCryptoProvider — a no-op pass-through that conforms to the same interface without performing any encryption:

Crypto = new CryptoOptions { Provider = NullCryptoProvider.Instance }

GDPR Inspection

The GDPR inspection report exposes the IsEncrypted flag for Art. 30 compliance documentation.

Performance Notes

  • AES-256-GCM is hardware-accelerated on all modern CPUs (AES-NI).
  • Each page is encrypted independently — random reads incur no extra I/O.
  • The GCM authentication tag is stored adjacent to each page for tamper detection.
  • Bulk inserts and WAL commits are unaffected in throughput beyond the encryption overhead (~3–5 % on modern hardware).
